text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- King Hussein says in Geneva that Jordan has translated its faith in peace into action. Calls for a halt to Jewish settlements and no change to demographics of Jerusalem.
- Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed says some political parties in Jordan are less than "political stalls", especially those who have loud voices but do little.
- Government to investigate the anarchy which broke out during English exams in Balqa governorate on Thursday when people broke into three exam halls and clashed with examiners.
- Murderer hanged at dawn this morning in Suwaqa jail for 1994 killing.
AL-DUSTOUR
- Crown Prince Hassan, visiting Turkey, says Iraq is not a case of security and oil, but of people.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali expected to visit Syria at the end of next month for talks with President Hafez al-Assad.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- King Hussein says Jordan hopes Jerusalem can be the capital of both Palestine and Israel.

- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says government not planning any changes to legislation on professional unions or parties. Says last month's press law had to be adopted to ensure that elections are held in a responsible atmosphere.
- Finance Minister Suleiman al-Hafez says financial compensation for bread purchases to be distributed tomorrow.
- Prime Minister Majali welcomes opening of Syrian border with Iraq; says Jordan is not egotistical and wants all Arab borders to be open.
AL-ASWAQ
- Companies expected to increase capital after cancellation of 15 tax on capital raises.
- Military court to hear final prosecution witnesses tomorrow in case of Jordanian soldier accused of murdering Israeli schoolgirls. Verdict expected during the next week.
JORDAN TIMES
- Crown Prince assured of Turkish army withdrawal from northern Iraq.
- First Jordanian satirical paper folds.
- Foul-play during English language school exam investigated.
